title: Finite relation fibre at a chart point gives etale quasi-compact residual self-relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $a:U\to X$ be a representable etale morphism from a scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Choose $u\in U$ and put $K=\kappa(u)=\mathcal O_{U,u}/\mathfrak m_u$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-field]. Write $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U\to X$ for its residue-field representative [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Form $R=U\times_XU$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and $E=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Suppose the set $\{r\in|R|:p_1(r)=u=p_2(r)\}$ is finite. Then both projections $E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ are etale and quasi-compact: their inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. No covering condition on $a$, finiteness of the fibre of $|U|\to|X|$, or quasi-compactness of $U$ is required.

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $i:T\to U$ be the canonical residue-field map. By [lem-sfb-residue-field-point-monomorphism], $i$ is monic. The representable diagonal in [def-trf-algebraic-space] makes $R$ and $E$ schemes; their sheaf fibre-product universal properties are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The induced $j:E\to R$ is monic: equality after $j$ makes both $U$-coordinates equal, cancellation through $i$ makes both $T$-coordinates equal, and the universal property then makes the original maps equal.

source.place: Tag 03JU (lemma-R-finite-above-x), first proof paragraph and implication (2) to (3).

proof.text: Monicity of $j$ gives injectivity on maps from every field spectrum. Apply the equivalence (1) implies (2) in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] to the scheme morphism $j$: it is universally injective, hence injective on underlying sets. Since $p_1j=i q_1$ and $p_2j=i q_2$, its image lies in $\{r:p_1(r)=u=p_2(r)\}$. The hypothesis therefore makes $|E|$ finite.

proof.text: A finite topological space is quasi-compact: from any open cover choose one member containing each point, giving a finite subcover. Hence step 2 makes $E$ quasi-compact by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. The field spectrum $T$ has only the opens $\varnothing$ and $T$, so the inverse images of its affine opens under either $q_\nu$ are $\varnothing$ or $E$. Both projections are therefore quasi-compact, as required.

tool_uses.why: Sheaf fibre-product existence and its universal property are generic constructions used for the chart relation, with no replacement of the unit route.
The scheme-theoretic fibre classification is applied to the two etale schemes over the field; the unit has no more specific scheme-fibre classification.
Open component inclusions of a scheme coproduct identify the subset-of-components map as an open immersion; this is a generic scheme construction.
Etaleness of open immersions and composition finishes each projection; this is generic morphism permanence, not a different direct-image argument.

The statement agrees with Stacks decent-spaces.tex Tag 03JU (lemma-R-finite-above-x): its first proof paragraph and the (2)=>(3) paragraph use only a finite self-pair fibre at the chosen chart point. I tested the statement on a Galois field chart, on A^1/Z at a closed point (holds), and at the generic point, where the hypothesis fails and E = coproduct over Z of Spec C(t) is not quasi-compact, so the hypothesis is necessary. Step 1: the residue-point monomorphism makes j: E->R monic by coordinatewise cancellation. Step 2: def-weil-radicial-morphism (1)=>(2) makes j injective on points, so |E| injects into the finite pair fibre. Step 3: representable etale gives h_nu: D_nu->T etale, and m_nu is monic. Step 4: the etale-fibre lemma writes D_nu as a disjoint union of finite separable field spectra, and the monomorphism-into-field-coproduct lemma (the 03DP step, infinite index sets allowed) identifies m_nu with a subset of components. Step 5: by the coproduct lemma m_nu is an open immersion, and composition-cancellation (1),(2) makes q_nu etale. Step 6: a finite space is quasi-compact and the opens of Spec K are only the empty set and Spec K, so both projections are quasi-compact. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. lean.statement: theorem chart_pair_finite_residual_relation {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (ha : IsEtale a) (u : U.left) (R : Over S) (p₁ p₂ : R ⟶ U) (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map p₁) (yoneda.map p₂) a a) (hfinite : Set.Finite {r : R.left | p₁.left r = u ∧ p₂.left r = u}) : ∃ (E : Over S) (q₁ q₂ : E ⟶ Over.mk (U.left.fromSpecResidueField u ≫ U.hom)), IsPullback (yoneda.map q₁) (yoneda.map q₂) (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U.left.fromSpecResidueField u) rfl) ≫ a) (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U.left.fromSpecResidueField u) rfl) ≫ a) ∧ (Etale q₁.left ∧ QuasiCompact q₁.left) ∧ (Etale q₂.left ∧ QuasiCompact q₂.left)
